PS1:air-race-championship.d: Air Race Championship is a racing game for the PlayStation, published by Xing Entertainment in 1999.

PS1:asterix-and-obelix-contro-cesare.d: Asterix & Obelix contro Cesare is an action / mini games game for the PlayStation, published by Cryo Interactive in 1999.

PS1:azito-2.d: Azito 2 is a strategy / constructing game for the PlayStation, published by Banpresto in 1998.

PS1:capcom-retro-game-collection-vol-1.d: Capcom Retro Game Collection Vol. 1 is a shooter game for the PlayStation, published by Capcom in 2005.

PS1:championship-motocross-featuring-ric.d: Championship Motocross Featuring Ricky Carmichael is a video game developed by Funcom Dublin and published by THQ for the PlayStation in 1999. It is the first of four motocross racing games published by THQ to be endorsed by professional motocross racer Ricky Carmichael. A sequel, Championship Motocross 2001 Featuring Ricky Carmichael, was released for Game Boy Color in 2000, and for PlayStation in 2001.

PS1:doukyuusei-mahjong.d: Doukyuusei Mahjong is a mahjong game for the PlayStation, published by Yumedia (Aroma) in 1997.

PS1:ebisu-yoshikazu-no-ooana-kyoutei.d: Ebisu Yoshikazu no Ooana Kyoutei is a kyōtei video game for the PlayStation, published by Seta Corporation in 1996.

PS1:jupiter-strike.d: Jupiter Strike (Zeitgeist in Japan) is a 3D rail shooter game for the PlayStation developed by Taito. Taito published the Japanese version, while Acclaim published the American and European version. A Microsoft Windows version was also released in 1996. The player takes control of a futuristic fighter jet that has two main weapons.

PS1:kids-station-mini-moni-ni-naru-no-da.st: Mini-Moni. ni Naru no da Pyon! (Controller Set)
PS1:kids-station-mini-moni-ni-naru-no-da.d: Kids Station: Mini-Moni. ni Naru no da Pyon! (Controller Set) is a mini games game for the PlayStation, published by Banpresto in 2002.

PS1:missland-2.d: Missland 2 is a puzzle game for the PlayStation, published by Altron in 1998.

PS1:ojousama-express.d: Ojousama Express is an adventure / dating game for the PlayStation, published by Media Works in 1998.

PS1:pachi-slot-teiou-2-kagetsu-2-pair-be.d: Pachi-Slot Teiou 2: Kagetsu - 2 Pair - Beaver X is a gambling game for the PlayStation, published by Mecko in 2000.

PS1:persona.d: Persona, previously marketed as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona outside of Japan, is a Japanese video game series and media franchise developed by Atlus and owned by Sega. Centered on a series of Japanese role-playing video games, Persona was originally conceived as a spin-off from Atlus' Megami Tensei franchise. The first entry in the series, Revelations: Persona, was released in 1996 for the PlayStation. The series has seen several more games since, with the most recent main entry being 2024's Persona 3 Reload, a remake of the 2006 game Persona 3.

PS1:pro-evolution-soccer-2.d: Pro Evolution Soccer 2 (abbreviated as PES 2), also known as World Soccer: Winning Eleven 6 outside of Europe, is the second installment of Konami's Pro Evolution Soccer football simulation video game series. The Japanese release was succeeded by an updated and improved version called World Soccer: Winning Eleven 6 Final Evolution. It was the last game in the series to be released for the PlayStation and the first and only game to be released for the GameCube, though it was the Japan-exclusive Final Evolution update. The cover of the Japanese version of the game featured Masashi Nakayama.

PS1:silhouette-stories.d: Silhouette Stories is a puzzle game for the PlayStation, published by Kaneko in 1996.

PS1:simple-1500-series-vol-73-the-invade.d: Simple 1500 Series Vol. 73: The Invaders - Space Invaders 1500 is an action / shooter game for the PlayStation, published by D3 Publisher in 2001.

PS1:slot-pro-6-hyper-juggler-v.d: Slot! Pro 6: Hyper Juggler V is a gambling game for the PlayStation, published by Nihon Telenet in 2002.

PS1:spyro-x-sparx-tondemo-tours.d: Spyro x Sparx: Tondemo Tours is an action / platformer game for the PlayStation, published by Sony in 2000.

PS1:super-adventure-rockman-disc-2-episo.t: Super Adventure Rockman (Disc 2) (Episode 2 Shitou! Wily Numbers)
PS1:super-adventure-rockman-disc-2-episo.d: Super Adventure Rockman is a 1998 interactive movie/rail shooter video game developed by Kouyousha and published by Capcom for the PlayStation and Sega Saturn; it is a spin-off of the Mega Man series and follows Mega Man as he attempts to stop an ancient alien supercomputer called "Ra Moon" from taking over the world. The game only saw a Japanese release and hasn't been re-released since. Considered darker than most Classic series games, Super Adventure Rockman has been met with mixed reception from media critics; Keiji Inafune, who worked on the series up until 2010, has also disowned the game, considering it one of the worst Mega Man games across the series.

PS1:super-robot-taisen-f-kanketsuhen.d: Super Robot Taisen F Kanketsuhen is a tactical rpg game for the PlayStation, published by Banpresto in 2000.

PS1:twisted-metal-3.d: Twisted Metal III is a 1998 vehicular combat video game developed and published by 989 Studios for the PlayStation. The game was released only in North America and was re-released for the Sony Greatest Hits line-up in 1999. It is the first installment not to be released in the PAL regions and published directly by Sony Computer Entertainment. Twisted Metal III is third in the Twisted Metal series and the first to be fully developed by 989 Studios.

PS1:v2000.d: V2000, also known as Virus 2000, is a 1998 video game developed by David Braben. The game was released on PlayStation and PC. It is a sequel to Zarch (also called Virus), and was intended to be less challenging than the original game.

PS1:worms-world-party.d: Worms World Party is a 2001 artillery turn-based tactics video game developed by Team17, and is the sequel to Worms Armageddon in the Worms series. As with the previous games in the series, players take turns controlling their teams and using available projectiles, firearms, explosives, and equipment to destroy all opposing teams and manoeuvre across a specified and highly destructible map. Although fairly well received upon release, the overall reception of Worms World Party has subsequently become mixed amongst the Worms community. Some found it to be an improvement to an already good game, whilst others saw it as being too derivative of its predecessor and not worthwhile for Worms…

PS2:buzz-the-music-quiz.d: Buzz!: The Music Quiz is a party music video game developed by Relentless Software and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the first instalment of the Buzz! series and was released exclusively in Europe and Australia. In The Music Quiz, players answer questions asked by the host, Buzz, by using the four Buzz!

PS2:crash-tag-team-racing.d: Crash Tag Team Racing is a 2005 kart racing and platform game developed by Radical Entertainment and published by Vivendi Universal Games (VU Games) for the PlayStation 2 (PS2), Xbox, GameCube, and PlayStation Portable (PSP). A version for the Nintendo DS by Sensory Sweep Studios was cancelled near its completion. It is the third racing game in the Crash Bandicoot video game series, following Crash Nitro Kart (2003). The game's story takes place in a racing-based theme park, in which Crash Bandicoot must recover its missing Power Gems to claim the park's ownership.

PS2:hametsu-no-mars.d: Hametsu no Mars is an adventure video game for the PlayStation 2, published by Idea Factory in 2005.

PS2:lord-of-the-rings-the-the-two-towers.w: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers (video game)
PS2:lord-of-the-rings-the-the-two-towers.d: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers is a 2002 hack and slash game developed by Stormfront Studios for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox. A 2D Game Boy Advance game of the same name was made by Griptonite Games, a port to the GameCube by Hypnos Entertainment, and to mobile by JAMDAT. A version for Microsoft Windows developed by Ritual Entertainment was cancelled during development. The game was published on all platforms by Electronic Arts. It is an adaption of the 2002 film of the same name.

PS2:reveal-fantasia.d: Reveal Fantasia: Mariel to Yousei Monogatari (リーヴェルファンタジア～マリエルと妖精物語～, Rīveru Fantajia: Marieru to Yousei Monogatari) is a Fantasy role playing video game released in 2002 for the PlayStation 2 console by Victor Interactive Software, Inc. in Japan. The game involved an innovative concept of a role playing game involving no battles or fighting. Its game play shows some influence from dating simulation games.

PS2:saru-get-you-2.d: Ape Escape 2 is a 2002 platform game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. The second main installment of the Ape Escape series, it was released in Japan in July 2002, Europe in March 2003 and North America in July 2003 by Ubi Soft. It received generally positive reviews from critics. The game was later used as the basis for the Ape Escape animated series by Frederator Studios.

PS2:simple-2000-series-vol-71-the-fantas.st: The Fantasy Renai Adventure - Kanojo no Densetsu

PS2:snow-white-and-the-7-clever-boys.t: Snow White and the 7 Clever Boys
PS2:snow-white-and-the-7-clever-boys.d: Snow White and the 7 Clever Boys is a game for the PlayStation 2, published by Phoenix Games Ltd. in 2006.

PS2:summer-athletics.d: Summer Athletics, also known as Summer Athletics: The Ultimate Challenge on the Xbox 360, in North America, is a sports game, developed by 49Games and published by Digital Entertainment Pool for the PlayStation 2, Wii, Xbox 360 and PC. The game features 28 events, which includes swimming, diving, archery and track cycling, as well as athletics. In the game, players can choose between two modes, the Arcade mode and the Realistic Mode, whereas players can choose difficulty from Amateur to Pro. Players may also have the opportunity to create, customize and name their own character and represent a country of their own.

PS2:top-gun-combat-zones.d: Top Gun: Combat Zones is a combat flight simulation game named after the 1986 film Top Gun. It was developed by British studio Digital Integration and published by Titus Interactive. It was originally released for the PlayStation 2 in 2001, followed by a GameCube version in 2002. Versions were also released for the Game Boy Advance and Microsoft Windows.

PS2:wacky-races-starring-dastardly-and-m.w: Wacky Races: Starring Dastardly and Muttley
PS2:wacky-races-starring-dastardly-and-m.d: Wacky Races: Starring Dastardly and Muttley is a 2000 kart racing game developed by Infogrames Sheffield House and published by Infogrames for the Dreamcast (under the title Wacky Races) and later for PlayStation 2 in 2001. The game is based on the cartoon series Wacky Races, which features 11 vehicles all racing over various landscapes to win first place. The vehicles featured include the most infamous vehicle in the series, the Mean Machine, driven by Dick Dastardly and Muttley.

PS3:go-diego-go-great-dinosaur-rescue.t: Go Diego Go! Great Dinosaur Rescue

PS3:mad-riders.d: Mad Riders is a racing video game for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, Microsoft Windows, and Mac OS X. It was developed by Techland and published by Ubisoft. Mad Riders was released in 2012. The game received mixed reviews upon its release, with critics praising the game's visuals but taking issue with its physics and controls.

PS3:nhl-10.d: NHL 10 is a video game in the NHL series developed and released by EA Canada and published by Electronic Arts, and is the 19th game in the series. The game debuted at Hockey Fest '09, a three-day interactive festival celebrating the sport of hockey and the Los Angeles Kings, which took place in downtown Los Angeles from August 28 to 30. On October 1, 2011, all online services for NHL 10 were discontinued.

PSP:2010-fifa-world-cup-south-africa.w: 2010 FIFA World Cup South Africa (video game)
PSP:2010-fifa-world-cup-south-africa.d: 2010 FIFA World Cup South Africa is the official video game for the 2010 FIFA World Cup, published by EA Sports and available to play on iOS and all major seventh-generation platforms except the Nintendo DS. Announced in January 2010 during an interview with one of the producers of the game, it was released 27 April 2010 in North America. 199 of the 204 teams that took part in the 2010 FIFA World Cup qualification are included in the game.
